bullets: How a letter can stand for an unknown number, and how a balanced scale solves x + 5 = 8
slides.heading: Algebra: letters stand for numbers, balanced scales
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we meet algebra - letters that stand for numbers, balanced scales that are equations, and how to solve x + 5 = 8 by undoing the +5 - and by the end you will be able to explain why x is a number, not a label.

bullets: Read a letter as an unknown number: x can stand for any number
See an equation as a balanced scale: both sides must weigh the same
Solve x + 5 = 8 by undoing the +5: x = 3
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things.

bullets: A classmate says 3x + 2x cannot be combined because x is just a label for boxes
Is that right? What does x really stand for?
slides.heading: Is x a label or a number?
slides.notes: Ask for a show of hands: can 3x + 2x be combined, or must something be wrong? Take two or three answers without judging them yet; say: hold on to your idea, because scene s4 settles this exactly.

bullets: A letter like x stands for an unknown number: it hides a number we do not know yet
An equation is a balanced scale: whatever is on the left must equal what is on the right
slides.heading: Letters stand for numbers: equations must balance
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: x hides a number, and an equation only works when both sides balance.

bullets: Think of x as a mystery box: the box holds a number - we just do not know which one yet
x could be 5, or 3, or 8: the letter stands in for whichever number fits
slides.heading: Letters can stand for unknown numbers
slides.notes: Point at the mystery boxes as they appear and narrate: each box hides a number, and x is the name we give that hidden number until we find it.

bullets: An equation is a balanced scale: whatever sits on the left must weigh the same as the right
If you change one side, you must do the same to the other side to keep the balance
slides.heading: A balanced scale is an equation
slides.notes: Narrate the scale slowly: left and right pans level because both sides weigh the same - that balance is what the equals sign means.

bullets: To find x, undo the +5: take 5 from both sides so the scale stays balanced
slides.heading: Solve x + 5 = 8 — undo the +5
slides.notes: Work the solving slowly: undo the +5 on the left by taking 5 from both sides, leaving x alone on one side and 3 on the other.

bullets: Careful - the trap is treating x as a label for things, so 3x + 2x cannot be combined
x stands for a number: 3x + 2x is 5x, like 3 mystery boxes plus 2 mystery boxes
slides.heading: Misconception: x is a number, not a label
slides.notes: Hold the claim up against the boxes: x is not a name tag for a thing - it stands for a number, so three lots of x plus two lots of x make five lots of x.

bullets: Undo the +5: take 5 from both sides, so x = 8 - 5
Answer: x = 3 - check: 3 + 5 = 8, so the scale balances
slides.heading: Worked example: solve x + 5 = 8
slides.notes: Talk through the undoing slowly as in scene s3 and name each step as you write it; say: checking 3 + 5 = 8 keeps the working honest.

bullets: Solve x + 4 = 9 by undoing the +4. Show both sides of the scale
Combine 3x + 2x and explain in one sentence why you can
slides.heading: Your turn: solve and combine
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them on undoing on both sides first, then on the exact sentence they used to explain why 3x + 2x is 5x.

bullets: On your own: solve x + 5 = 8 and show the undoing step
Explain in one sentence why x is a number, not a label
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the undo-the-+5 working in your first answer, plus one clear sentence about x standing for a number in your second.
